commons:8943891.summary: In a lunette of the crypt at Hosios Loukas, the body of Christ is laid out on a slab, the Virgin bending close over him while two mourners and a winged angel attend on the right. Painted for the burial crypt beneath the monastery church, the scene of Christ's burial had a special meaning in a place of tombs, where the monks awaited the resurrection he made possible.
facts: The crypt has eight lunettes with scenes of Christ's Passion and Resurrection, together with forty medallion portraits of apostles, martyrs and abbots.
The frescoes are believed to date mostly after 1048 and the death of Theodore Leobachus, a patron who became abbot.
Hidden under centuries of dust, the paintings were cleaned by the Greek Archaeological Service in the 1960s.
commons:8943891.notes: The scene could also be read as a Lamentation; the Commons category names it the Entombment.
